The Unexpected Factors

In the real world, things don't always go as planned. These are the random events that can boost or hinder your projects, reflecting political, economic, or logistical challenges.

Positive Modifiers

State Infrastructure Investment

A new state-funded project provides additional resources and expertise, accelerating your progress and reducing costs. This reflects how major government funding can dramatically improve local projects.

+2 Resilience +1 Trust

Efficient Supply Chain

Materials and equipment are delivered ahead of schedule due to strong relationships with suppliers and efficient logistics, allowing for faster implementation of your solutions.

+1 Resilience +0 Trust

Unexpected Philanthropy

A local company or wealthy resident donates a significant sum to the cause, helping you cover costs and expand the reach of your project. This demonstrates the role of private funding in public works.

+1 Resilience +2 Trust

Negative Modifiers

NIMBY Citizens

("Not In My Backyard") A highly vocal group of citizens protests the new construction, causing delays and public friction. This highlights the political challenges of building infrastructure.

-1 Resilience -2 Trust

Materials Shortage

A global or regional shortage of a key building material (e.g., steel or concrete) drives up costs and delays your project. This shows how local projects are affected by a larger, global economy.

-2 Resilience -1 Trust

Labor Strike

Workers' unions go on strike to demand better wages and conditions. This halts all construction and public operations, demonstrating the power of labor movements.

-1 Resilience -2 Trust
